_comment: Per-OS text variants applied by tools/build_os.py. Each entry names the files (relative to the v2 root), the exact master text (must occur exactly once in each listed file unless optional=true), and the replacement per OS. A null value keeps the master text; the special key 'all' is used for the all-platform master build.

variants.match: Ubuntu/Debian, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Windows 11 via WSL 2 Ubuntu.
variants.ubuntu: **Ubuntu/Debian edition** (22.04+ / Debian 12; the macOS and Windows 11 editions are separate downloads).
variants.macos: **macOS edition** (Intel & Apple Silicon; the Ubuntu/Debian and Windows 11 editions are separate downloads).
variants.windows: **Windows 11 edition** (inside WSL 2 Ubuntu; the Ubuntu/Debian and macOS editions are separate downloads).

variants.match: # Bash Scripting — zero to hero, project-based · Full Trainer Edition

variants.match: Supported platforms, the same as the rest of the program: **Ubuntu/Debian** (22.04 or later; any terminal), **macOS** (Intel or Apple Silicon; Terminal or iTerm), **Windows 11** — *inside WSL 2 Ubuntu*: every command in this course is typed in the Ubuntu terminal that WSL gives you, never in PowerShell. (Windows 11 support added 2026-10-21; before that the course was published for **macOS** and **Ubuntu**.)
variants.ubuntu: This is the **Ubuntu/Debian edition** (22.04 or later, Debian 12; any terminal). The macOS and Windows 11 editions of the course are separate; the content is identical except for setup and a few platform notes.
variants.macos: This is the **macOS edition** (Intel or Apple Silicon; Terminal or iTerm). The Ubuntu/Debian and Windows 11 editions of the course are separate; the content is identical except for setup and a few platform notes.
variants.windows: This is the **Windows 11 edition** — everything runs *inside WSL 2 Ubuntu*: every command in this course is typed in the Ubuntu terminal that WSL gives you, never in PowerShell. The Ubuntu/Debian and macOS editions are separate; the content is identical except for setup and a few platform notes.

variants.match: 1) **Windows 11 only, first:** in an administrator PowerShell run `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`, reboot, open the *Ubuntu* app and create your Linux user; from here on you are on Ubuntu, and the course folder must live under your Linux home (`~/`), not under `/mnt/c/…`. 2) Install Docker. **macOS:** Docker Desktop (Intel or Apple Silicon build). **Ubuntu/Debian, and WSL 2 Ubuntu:** Docker Engine and the Compose plugin from Docker's apt repository (the `docker-ce`, `docker-ce-cli`, `containerd.io` and `docker-compose-plugin` packages); on Windows 11 you may instead install Docker Desktop for Windows and enable its *WSL 2 integration* for the Ubuntu distro — either way `docker` is run from the Ubuntu terminal. Follow the current official installation page for your OS (`docs.docker.com`); the full step-by-step commands for each OS — adding Docker's apt repository, the `docker` group, enabling systemd in WSL 2, and the Docker Desktop alternative — are on the **Environment (Docker) — setup, step by step** page (`env/README.md`, sections 2–4); do that page first if Docker is not installed yet. 3) Start Docker (the Desktop app on macOS or Windows; `sudo systemctl start docker` on Ubuntu — inside WSL 2, `sudo service docker start` if `systemctl` is not available). 4) Run:
variants.ubuntu: 1) Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin from Docker's apt repository (the `docker-ce`, `docker-ce-cli`, `containerd.io`, `docker-buildx-plugin` and `docker-compose-plugin` packages) — the exact commands are on the **Environment (Docker) — setup, step by step** page (`env/README.md`, section 2); do that page first if Docker is not installed yet. 2) Add yourself to the `docker` group and log out and back in. 3) Start Docker: `sudo systemctl enable --now docker`. 4) Run:
variants.macos: 1) Install Docker Desktop for Mac (Intel or Apple Silicon build — check *About This Mac*) — the exact steps are on the **Environment (Docker) — setup, step by step** page (`env/README.md`, section 3); do that page first if Docker is not installed yet. 2) Open Docker from Applications and wait for **Engine running**. 3) Open Terminal. 4) Run:
variants.windows: 1) **First:** in an administrator PowerShell run `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`, reboot, open the *Ubuntu* app and create your Linux user; from here on you are on Ubuntu, and the course folder must live under your Linux home (`~/`), not under `/mnt/c/…`. 2) Inside the Ubuntu window install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin from Docker's apt repository, and enable systemd so the daemon starts with WSL — the exact commands are on the **Environment (Docker) — setup, step by step** page (`env/README.md`, sections 2 and 4); you may instead install Docker Desktop for Windows and enable its *WSL 2 integration* for the Ubuntu distro — either way `docker` is run from the Ubuntu terminal. 3) Start Docker (`sudo systemctl enable --now docker` with systemd enabled; otherwise `sudo service docker start` each time you open Ubuntu; with Docker Desktop, just open it). 4) Run:

variants.match: *Server missing on macOS:* start Docker Desktop and wait for "Engine running". *Server missing on Ubuntu:* `sudo systemctl start docker`; `permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket` → `sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"`, then log out and back in. *`docker compose` unknown on Ubuntu* → the `docker-compose-plugin` package is missing (the old `docker-compose` v1 binary and the `docker.io` distro package are not what this course uses). *WSL 2:* `wsl --install` fails or Ubuntu will not start → virtualization is disabled in the BIOS/UEFI, or `wsl --update` is needed first; Docker Desktop's WSL integration toggle is under *Settings → Resources → WSL integration*. `bad interpreter` or `^M` errors in a file you edited from Windows → the editor saved CRLF line endings; set it to LF (VS Code: the `CRLF`/`LF` switch in the status bar). *Going on to Course 1 on Windows 11:* WSL 2 needs the Hyper-V hypervisor, and Course 1 Module 0 asks you to turn it off (`bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off`) for a faster VirtualBox — do that only after Course 0, and turn it back on (`… auto`) when you need WSL 2 again; or keep Hyper-V on and accept a slower lab VM; or run Course 0 inside the Course 1 lab VM, which has no such conflict. If still blocked after 30 min, use the **fallback** in `env/README.md` §8 for M00–M08 and return to Docker before M09.
variants.ubuntu: *Server missing:* `sudo systemctl start docker`; `permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket` → `sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"`, then log out and back in. *`docker compose` unknown* → the `docker-compose-plugin` package is missing (the old `docker-compose` v1 binary and the `docker.io` distro package are not what this course uses). If still blocked after 30 min, use the **fallback** in `env/README.md` §8 for M00–M08 and return to Docker before M09.
variants.macos: *Server missing:* start Docker Desktop and wait for "Engine running" (the whale in the menu bar stops animating). *`docker compose` unknown* → update Docker Desktop; the Compose plugin ships with it. *Docker Desktop will not start:* System Settings → Privacy & Security may be waiting for you to allow it. If still blocked after 30 min, use the **fallback** in `env/README.md` §8 for M00–M08 and return to Docker before M09.
variants.windows: *Server missing:* `sudo systemctl start docker` (systemd enabled) or `sudo service docker start`; with Docker Desktop, open it and check that *Settings → Resources → WSL integration* is on for Ubuntu. `permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket` → `sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"`, then `wsl --shutdown` from PowerShell and reopen Ubuntu. *`docker compose` unknown* → the `docker-compose-plugin` package is missing. `wsl --install` fails or Ubuntu will not start → virtualization is disabled in the BIOS/UEFI, or `wsl --update` is needed first. `bad interpreter` or `^M` errors in a file you edited from Windows → the editor saved CRLF line endings; set it to LF (VS Code: the `CRLF`/`LF` switch in the status bar). *Going on to Course 1:* WSL 2 needs the Hyper-V hypervisor, and Course 1 Module 0 asks you to turn it off (`bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off`) for a faster VirtualBox — do that only after Course 0, and turn it back on (`… auto`) when you need WSL 2 again; or keep Hyper-V on and accept a slower lab VM; or run Course 0 inside the Course 1 lab VM, which has no such conflict. If still blocked after 30 min, use the **fallback** in `env/README.md` §8 for M00–M08 and return to Docker before M09.

variants.match: `sed: 1: … invalid command code` or a `-i` error on macOS → BSD `sed`: the GNU tools are not first on `PATH` (Environment section 3 step 6); fix that, or write `sed -i '' 's/…/…/'`.

`flock: command not found` on macOS → `flock` is util-linux, which macOS does not ship; install the Homebrew port (`brew install flock`, Environment section 3 step 6) and rerun — the lock is then real on a Mac too. If you cannot install it, run the two probe lines in the course container and note in your runbook that the lock was verified on Linux only.

variants.windows: `flock: command not found` on macOS → `flock` is util-linux (installed in WSL 2 Ubuntu by default; on a Mac, run this step in the course container and note in your runbook that the lock is Linux-only).

> path for M00–M08 and defer Docker to M09.
